title: Harmonize benchmark runners, CUDA/driver pinning, and image catalog for stable tokens/sec baselines
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Our end-to-end load tests for tokens/sec and p95 latency show noisy variance across CI runs caused by mismatched driver/CUDA versions, inconsistent pinned runtime images, and divergent runner configurations (container runtime, cgroup settings, NUMA/locality). Goal: Produce a minimal, reproducible set of pinned images and runner configs that bring tokens/sec baselines within +/-3% run-to-run variance and allow deterministic p95 tracking and regression detection. Scope: standardize pinned CUDA and NVIDIA driver versions for all benchmark images, publish an image catalog (stable/reproducible tags), introduce a canonical runner profile used by CI and by on-prem benchmarking hosts, and update the regression detector to record environment metadata so we can filter/triage environment-induced noise.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible image catalog with pinned CUDA and driver combinations is published and referenced by all benchmark jobs
CI benchmark runs across 10 sample rigs show tokens/sec variance <= 3% and p95 variance consistent with historical noise model
Benchmark job templates in repo use the canonical runner profile and surface environment metadata in logs and metrics
Regression detection alerts include environment tags and suppress false positives tied to non-standard drivers or images
Documentation and onboarding guide for adding new runner hardware or image variants published to Confluence
updates: 2026-02-11: Kickoff meeting with infra, runtime, and perf-research. Agreed scope and target variance threshold (+/-3%). Assigned owner for image catalog.

2026-02-16: Proof-of-concept: built 3 pinned images (cuda-11.8+nvidia-525, cuda-12.1+nvidia-535, cuda-12.2+nvidia-545) with identical runtime deps. Initial tokens/sec runs show 6-8% spread on a mixed fleet.

2026-02-20: Infra suggested standardizing on cuda-12.1+nvidia-535 for hosted CI due to driver stability and availability on our cloud images. Noted potential perf differences for quantized kernels; perf-research to validate.
2026-02-24: Implemented canonical runner profile (runc v1, cgroup v2, cpu isolation flags, NUMA-aware cpuset). Deployed to canary CI pool and ran 50+ synthetic batches.
2026-02-27: Metric plumbing added: benchmark_runner_env tag on tokens/sec and latency metrics; Grafana dashboard updated to allow environment filtering.

2026-03-01: First integration with regression detector: detector now records image_digest, cuda_version, driver_version. Detector suppressed 2 historical alerts retroactively after correlating to older driver variants. Follow-up: add automated image digest check into PR gating.
notes_and_tradeoffs: Trade-offs considered: pinning to a single CUDA/driver reduces noise but may penalize newer hardware that benefits from newer drivers. Decided on a matrix approach: canonical CI images (single pair) + optional hardware-specific catalog entries that require an approval step. We will measure quantized kernel delta and document expected deltas per image in the catalog. Also evaluated using container-aware GPU sharing vs dedicated GPUs; chosen dedicated for benchmark consistency.
